zone.name: Mount Geigerich Area
zone.description: Mount Giegerich is located close to Lemon Pass and is accessed via Griffin Creek. It will take you a few hours to get over to this summit but the views of this area are worth the walk as is the skiing.

routes.name: Molly's Elevens
routes.description: Mount Giegerich summit is 2,249 metres and offers up great views of the West side of Kokanee Glacier Park. The ascent is gentle as is the ski down but be aware of cornices forming on the ridge. To access Mount Giegerich from Kokanee Glacier Cabin head West across Kaslo Lake and skin up the low point which is where Griffin Creek empties into Kaslo Lake. It is a relatively steep 160 meter climb and then things flatten out. Follow this valley as if to ascend Nansen Mountain but instead head more Southwesterly to the peak directly South on the same ridge line. There is a sparsely tree ridge line that you can follow to the summit staying well away of the steeper Skol route on Giegerich's more northerly side. From the summit Molly's Eleven route is the most direct line back down more-or-less the way you ascended. It's a long, mellow heli-ski type route so enjoy. The way back to the cabin is the exact way you came so simply follow your tracks.
routes.notes: Placement: summit = BCGNIS/ATES Mt Giegerich, DEM top 2434 m, not the guide's 2,249 m (the guide's 500 m gain from the cabin fits ~2430 m, so the printed height looks wrong). Skin: across Kaslo Lake to the Griffin Creek mouth on the W shore, the ~165 m climb to ~2125 m, the flat Griffin valley SW to the basin head (~2200 m), S onto the summit's E shoulder (taken as the sparsely treed ridge) and W up it to the top. Descent: back down the shoulder (just N of the skin), into the basin and down Griffin Creek to Kaslo Lake (475 m). All MRDEM-30, so confidence is capped at medium.

routes.name: Mount Giegerich - Skol
routes.description: Mount Giegerich summit is 2,249 metres and offers up great views of the West side of Kokanee Glacier Park. The ascent is gentle as is the ski down but be aware of cornices forming on the ridge. To access Mount Giegerich from Kokanee Glacier Cabin head West across Kaslo Lake and skin up the low point which is where Griffin Creek empties into Kaslo Lake. It is a relatively steep 160 meter climb and then things flatten out. Follow this valley as if to ascend Nansen Mountain but instead head more Southwesterly to the peak directly South on the same ridge line. There is a sparsely tree ridge line that you can follow to the summit staying well away of the steeper Skol route on Giegerich's more northerly side. From the summit Skol is just to the North of the summit and the treed ridge which you likely ascended. Caution is required skiing this route as it is steep and typically Corniced, you will want to ski it one at a time and only in stable conditions. The way back to the Kokanee Glacier Cabin is the exact way you came so simply follow your tracks.
routes.notes: Placement: summit = BCGNIS/ATES Mt Giegerich, DEM top 2434 m, not the guide's 2,249 m (the guide's 500 m gain from the cabin fits ~2430 m, so the printed height looks wrong). Skin: across Kaslo Lake to the Griffin Creek mouth on the W shore, the ~165 m climb to ~2125 m, the flat Griffin valley SW to the basin head (~2200 m), S onto the summit's E shoulder (taken as the sparsely treed ridge) and W up it to the top. Descent (Skol): from the summit ~150 m N along the crest, then NE down the steeper N/NE slope (25-34 deg on MRDEM, steeper in reality) into the Griffin basin at ~2211 m (~225 m). Exact line and cornice not resolvable on MRDEM-30. FLAG: the vertical check is about -55 to -60% against gain_m 500, because that figure is the climb from the cabin, not this face; the return is down the shared skin track (Griffin Creek) to Kaslo Lake, so the line was not stretched to match.

routes.name: Mount Giegerich - East Face
routes.description: Mount Giegerich summit is 2,249 metres and offers up great views of the West side of Kokanee Glacier Park. The ascent is gentle as is the ski down but be aware of cornices forming on the ridge. To access Mount Giegerich from Kokanee Glacier Cabin head West across Kaslo Lake and skin up the low point which is where Griffin Creek empties into Kaslo Lake. It is a relatively steep 160 meter climb and then things flatten out. Follow this valley as if to ascend Nansen Mountain but instead head more Southwesterly to the peak directly South on the same ridge line. There is a sparsely tree ridge line that you can follow to the summit staying well away of the steeper Skol route on Giegerich's more northerly side. From the summit the East face is the large bowl to the south of the treed ridge line you ascended and just south of Molly's Elevens. There is plenty of room on the East Face to ski it lap after lap, the pitch is not steep but it is sustained. The way back to the Kokanee Glacier Cabin is the exact way you came so simply follow your tracks.
routes.notes: Placement: summit = BCGNIS/ATES Mt Giegerich, DEM top 2434 m, not the guide's 2,249 m (the guide's 500 m gain from the cabin fits ~2430 m, so the printed height looks wrong). Descent (East Face): the E-facing slope S of the shoulder, from the summit to the flats at ~2232 m (~200 m, 13-24 deg sustained). The bowl's extent is uncertain on MRDEM-30. FLAG: the vertical check is about -55 to -60% against gain_m 500, because that figure is the climb from the cabin, not this face; the return is down the shared skin track (Griffin Creek) to Kaslo Lake, so the line was not stretched to match.
